description: Helios fidelity threshold for alpha=4 force detection: noise model analysis for chi=3 8q MERA

circuit.note: estimated from chi=3 SU(4) decomposition, 2-layer MERA

hypothesis_claim: Force detection feasible at dr=1..4 at Helios 99.921%
key_finding: Hypothesis PARTIALLY REFUTED. Helios 99.921% achieves dr_max=2, not dr_max=4 as claimed. dr=3 (SNR=1.9x) falls below the 3-sigma threshold. A 2-point fit (dr=1,2) is insufficient to establish a power law. The hypothesis overestimated the signal amplitude at dr=3..4 by factor ~2x.
correction: For 4-point alpha fit (dr=1..4), fidelity threshold is ~99.97-99.99% per gate (not 99.5% as hypothesized). Helios is insufficient for power-law detection. FT neutral atoms or error-corrected hardware required.
what_is_confirmed: dr=1 (SNR 44x) and dr=2 (SNR 10x) are cleanly detectable on Helios. This is sufficient to confirm the EXISTENCE of attractive holographic forces but not to fit the power-law exponent.
recommendation: Helios run: target dr=1..2 only as a force-existence proof. Frame as 'detecting holographic attraction' not 'measuring power-law exponent'. Full alpha measurement requires FT hardware.
